factions.name: Working Families
factions.who: Union households, factory towns, service workers

factions.name: Green Future
factions.who: Climate voters, young professionals, outdoorsy states

factions.name: Innovators
factions.who: Engineers, founders and the cities they build

factions.name: Security First
factions.who: Veterans, military towns, the defence industry

factions.name: Civil Rights Coalition
factions.who: Black and Latino civic groups, churches and unions

planks.name: Social Security Lockbox
planks.blurb: Wall off the surplus: every dollar of payroll tax pays down debt until the boomers retire.

planks.name: Medicare Drug Benefit
planks.blurb: Prescription coverage for every senior, through Medicare.

planks.name: Across-the-Board Tax Cut
planks.blurb: Cut every income bracket; return the surplus to the people who paid it.

planks.name: Standards & Testing
planks.blurb: Test every child, publish every school's results, fund the schools that improve.

planks.name: Ratify Kyoto
planks.blurb: Send the climate treaty to the Senate and fight for 67 votes.

planks.name: Broadband for Every County
planks.blurb: Federal loans to wire rural America for high-speed internet.

planks.name: Missile Defence
planks.blurb: Build a national missile shield; leave the ABM treaty if needed.

planks.name: Trade With China (PNTR)
planks.blurb: Permanent normal trade relations with China ahead of its entry to the WTO.

planks.name: AI Transition Fund
planks.blurb: Wage insurance and retraining for workers displaced by AI, paid for by a levy on large compute.

planks.name: Carbon Dividend
planks.blurb: A rising fee on carbon; every dollar comes back to households as a quarterly cheque.

planks.name: Border & Fentanyl Act
planks.blurb: Four thousand agents, scanners at every port of entry, and asylum courts that decide in months.

planks.name: Housing Abundance Act
planks.blurb: Federal money for towns that legalise apartments near jobs and transit.

planks.name: Medicine Price Cap
planks.blurb: Cap what patients pay for insulin, GLP-1s and cancer drugs at $200 a month.

planks.name: Family Tax Credit
planks.blurb: $3,000 a child, paid monthly, to working and non-working parents alike.

planks.name: Arsenal Act
planks.blurb: Rebuild the shipyards and triple munitions output before 2031.

planks.name: Reshoring Tariffs
planks.blurb: A 15% tariff on imports from strategic rivals; the revenue funds new factories.

policies.name: Big Tent
policies.text: Faction friendship fades half as fast.

policies.name: Realignment
policies.text: Finisher: allied factions' heartlands shift your way each turn.

policies.name: The Machine
policies.text: Finisher: every HQ pushes three rings out.

policies.name: Clean Campaign
policies.text: +2 Momentum a turn; scandals are rarer.

century.name: Commercial internet
century.note: Email, the web, the first online shops.

century.name: Broadband
century.note: Always-on internet in most homes. Unlocks online video and social media.

century.name: Social media
century.note: The feed arrives. Scandals travel in hours, not days.

century.name: Smartphones
century.note: A computer in every pocket. The press goes mobile.

century.name: Deep learning
century.note: Machines learn to see and hear.

century.name: Language models
century.note: AI writes and codes. The first labour-shock forecasts.

century.name: AI agents
century.note: Software that does office work end to end.

century.name: Self-driving freight
century.note: 3.5 million driving jobs at risk; freight costs fall 20–35%.

century.name: General-purpose robots
century.note: Robots in warehouses, kitchens and care homes.

century.name: AI-run research
century.note: AI systems run experiments. Every other lane speeds up.

century.name: Transformative AI?
century.note: The widest forecast in the game. The forecast itself is a political issue.

century.name: AI Transition Fund
century.note: Wage insurance and retraining. Softens the labour shock.

century.name: Automation dividend
century.note: A share of automation profits paid to every adult. Needs: General-purpose robots.

century.name: Combined-cycle gas
century.note: Efficient gas plants replace old coal.

century.name: Hydrogen cars
century.note: Much hyped. Historically, it did not arrive; the forecast says so.

century.name: Shale drilling
century.note: Cheap gas. America becomes an energy exporter; coal declines.

century.name: Solar at grid parity
century.note: Solar becomes the cheapest new power in most states.

century.name: Mass-market electric cars
century.note: Petrol demand peaks.

century.name: Grid batteries
century.note: Sunshine at night. Wind and solar firm up.

century.name: Enhanced geothermal
century.note: Clean power anywhere you can drill.

century.name: Small modular reactors
century.note: Factory-built nuclear plants.

century.name: Carbon removal at scale
century.note: Pulling CO₂ out of the air for under $150 a tonne.

century.name: Fusion pilot plant
century.note: The first plant to put fusion power on the grid. Maybe.

century.name: Carbon price
century.note: Every tonne pays. Emissions fall; petrol rises.

century.name: HIV antiretrovirals
century.note: A death sentence becomes a chronic illness.

century.name: Human genome
century.note: The map of human DNA, finished.

century.name: Gene editing
century.note: Cut and paste DNA. Cures, and new ethics fights.

century.name: mRNA vaccines
century.note: A vaccine designed in two days.

century.name: GLP-1 drugs
century.note: Obesity falls; health spending bends.

century.name: AI diagnosis
century.note: Better than most doctors at reading scans.

century.name: Cancer vaccines
century.note: Personalised vaccines against tumours.

century.name: Ageing drugs
century.note: Healthy lifespan +3–6 years. Pensions strain.

century.name: Lab-grown organs
century.note: No more transplant waiting lists.

century.name: Medicine price cap
century.note: Caps what patients pay for key drugs.

century.name: Precision weapons
century.note: GPS-guided munitions.

century.name: Armed drones
century.note: War by remote control.

century.name: Cyber command
century.note: The fifth domain of war.

century.name: Hypersonic missiles
century.note: Too fast to intercept, for now.

century.name: Drone swarms
century.note: Thousands of cheap drones, one mind.

century.name: Space missile tracking
century.note: Satellites that see every launch.

century.name: Quantum-safe encryption
century.note: Secrets that survive the quantum computer.

century.name: Laser missile defence
century.note: Shooting down missiles for dollars a shot.

century.name: Code-breaking quantum computer
century.note: Every unprotected secret becomes readable.

century.name: Autonomous weapons treaty
century.note: A human decides every strike. If the others sign.

era.agenda: Wants: entry to the World Trade Organization
Wants: respect, and no NATO in the Baltics
Wants: a climate treaty with teeth
Wants: an end to its lost decade
Wants: the sanctions lifted after its nuclear tests
Wants: a seat at the top table

term.agenda: Wants: Taiwan, on its own timetable
Wants: sanctions lifted, Ukraine settled on its terms
Wants: a trade truce and AI rules
Wants: a firmer line in the Strait
Wants: chip factories, and a free hand

units.role: Your candidate: a stump speech moves a whole region; the campaign plane flies anywhere once a turn.
The running mate: rallies like a surrogate, twice as hard at home.
Knocks doors, opens field offices and new state HQs.
A well-known supporter on tour: rallies move two rings of hexes.
A poll replaces the public polls' guess with the truth in that state, and feeds the think tank.
Buys airtime: moves every hex in the state it stands in, or targets a rival unit.
Fights over the rules: wins contests, and decides recounts.
A legend of the trade, with one great move.

unit.name: Advance Team
unit.text: Replaces the organizer line. +1 move; canvassing 25% stronger.

ability.name: Floor Leader
ability.text: Doctrines cost 15% less Influence; laws are built 25% faster.

unit.name: Committee Staffer
unit.text: Replaces the pollster line. Every poll also gives +3 Ideas.

ability.name: Chain of Command
ability.text: All units +1 move. Security First starts as your ally.

unit.name: Veterans Brigade
unit.text: Replaces the surrogate line. Rallies 30% stronger, double where Security First is strong.

ability.name: Venture Capital
ability.text: Start with $30 more. Every HQ makes +2 Ideas.

unit.name: Growth Team
unit.text: Replaces the ad line. Ads spill into neighbouring states at half strength.

ability.name: Movement
ability.text: Field offices push twice as hard. Canvassing reaches one more ring.

unit.name: Block Captain
unit.text: Replaces the organizer line. Opens field offices without being used up.

ability.name: City Hall
ability.text: Every push is 50% stronger on city hexes.

unit.name: Precinct Captain
unit.text: Replaces the organizer line. Canvassing a city hex counts double.

ideas.name: Cable Strategy
ideas.text: Ads 25% stronger. Unlocks the TV Studio.

ideas.name: Tracking Polls
ideas.text: Every poll gives +2 Ideas and reaches one state further.

ideas.name: Microtargeting
ideas.text: Canvassing 25% stronger. Unlocks the Data Lab.

ideas.name: Social Media Campaigns
ideas.text: Ads spill into neighbouring states at half strength.

ideas.name: Big Data Turnout
ideas.text: +1.5 points on Election Day in every state you lead by under 3.

ideas.name: Rapid Response
ideas.text: Scandals and bad nights cost half as much.

ideas.name: Vote-by-Mail Operations
ideas.text: Each field office adds +1 on Election Day (up to +2 a state).

buildings.name: TV Studio
buildings.text: +1 Influence, +$1; ad teams built here cost half.

laws.name: Aviation Security Act
laws.text: Locked cockpit doors, watch lists at check-in, federal screeners. Dull and expensive, until it is not.

laws.name: Medicare Drug Benefit
laws.text: Prescription coverage for every senior, through Medicare.

laws.name: Across-the-Board Tax Cut
laws.text: Cut every bracket; return the surplus to the people who paid it.

laws.name: Broadband for Every County
laws.text: Federal loans to wire rural America.

laws.name: Standards and Testing Act
laws.text: Test every child; fund the schools that improve.

laws.name: National Energy Plan
laws.text: New transmission lines, a strategic power reserve and help for California.

laws.name: Patients' Bill of Rights
laws.text: The right to see a specialist, and to sue your health plan.

events.body: The year is 2000. The computers survived the millennium; the stock market has doubled in eighteen months; the outgoing President is from your party and the country is at peace. {leader} of {leader_state} means to keep it that way. Ahead lie fifty years nobody can see: wars, crashes, machines that think. The {party} Party will live through all of it, or not.

events.title: The computers held
events.sub: Y2K passes quietly. Markets open at records: the Nasdaq is up 86% in a year. The {party} Party holds the White House; the {rival_party} Party has its candidate in {rival}.

events.kicker: New Hampshire · three weeks to the primary
events.title: An insurgent in the snow
events.body: {challenger}, {challenger_office}, is running against you for the nomination on behalf of {weakest_name}, who say the party takes them for granted. A loss in New Hampshire would wound you. A long fight would wound the party.
events.advice: Their demand costs little with the other factions. Fighting is close to a coin toss.

choices.label: Adopt their demand: {weakest_demand_name}
choices.text: They stand down and endorse you. The pledge costs no Influence.

result.title: {challenger_last} endorses you
result.body: The {weakest_demand_name} goes into your platform. {weakest_name} are back on side.

choices.label: Fight them in New Hampshire
choices.text: Win and the challenge is over; lose and it drags into spring.

result.body_win: The challenge is over. The faction is not happy.
result.body_lose: The fight goes on to Super Tuesday, and it costs money and goodwill.

choices.label: Promise them a cabinet post
choices.text: A deal in a hotel room. They stand down; you owe them in 2001.

result.title: {challenger_last} stands down
result.body: {challenger} will expect a seat at the cabinet table.

events.title: The dot-com bubble
events.body: The Nasdaq has doubled in eighteen months on companies with no profits. The Fed chair wants political cover to lean against it before it pops.

lines.label: Chance the Nasdaq falls 30% or more
Growth in 2001 if it does, with no action
Growth in 2001 if it does, cooled now

choices.label: Back the Fed
choices.text: Slower growth now (−0.3 nationally); a softer landing when it comes.

choices.label: Let the boom run
choices.text: Nothing now. The forecast stands.

events.title: Tech slides; no panic
events.sub: The Nasdaq falls 24% from its March peak. Economists credit the Fed's early warning.

events.title: The bubble bursts
events.sub: The Nasdaq loses 37% in five weeks. Two trillion dollars of paper wealth, gone. Your party holds the White House, and owns the economy in November.

events.title: Who writes the platform?
events.body: The platform committee meets in a hotel ballroom with three hundred delegates and one draft. How much of it is yours?

choices.label: Write it yourself
choices.text: +12 Influence to spend on pledges. The factions grumble (−3 each).

choices.label: Let the factions write it
choices.text: Every allied faction +8 friendship.

choices.label: Keep it short and vague
choices.text: +2 Momentum. Nobody is offended; nobody is inspired.

events.title: Choose a running mate
events.body: The running mate joins the board as a unit: a second candidate who rallies twice as hard in their home state. What they hide you find out by vetting, or in October.

events.title: The nomination is yours
events.body: Twenty thousand delegates, a week of speeches, and a party that fought you through the primaries. Tonight you accept its nomination. The speech sets the tone for the fall.

choices.label: Hope: one country, one future
choices.text: Broad and warm: +1.0 nationally, +2 Momentum.

choices.label: Fight: name what is wrong
choices.text: Your factions love it (+10 each); swing voters less so (+0.2 nationally).

choices.label: The plan for day one
choices.text: Dry, but it reads well: +0.6 nationally, +8 Ideas.

events.title: Nine weeks to go
events.sub: From now on, each turn is two weeks. Every rally, every ad and every faction counts double the attention.

events.title: The {third_name} is on the ballot
events.body: {third_name}, the party of {third_faction} voters you lost, is polling {third_share}% in its strongest states. Every vote it wins there could have been yours.

choices.label: Court their voters
choices.text: {third_faction} +15 friendship; if they come back, the third party fades.

choices.label: Attack them as spoilers
choices.text: Their share falls by a third; their voters remember (−5).

choices.label: Ignore them
choices.text: Spend nothing on it.

events.kicker: Boston · the first debate · 46 million watching
events.title: The first debate
events.body: {rival} has spent a week at debate camp. Your team has three plans for the night. The odds come from your ratings.

choices.label: Go deep on the plan
choices.text: A policy night. Big if it works; dull if not.

choices.label: Land the line
choices.text: One sentence that leads every newscast.

choices.label: Stay steady
choices.text: No mistakes, no headlines.

events.title: The story about {mate}
events.body: Business records: a consulting firm, a foreign client, fees nobody disclosed. The story runs at six.

choices.label: Stand by {mate_first}
choices.text: Loyal. The story runs for a week.

choices.label: Release everything tonight
choices.text: A gamble that the details are dull.

choices.label: Prove it is a fake
choices.text: Your forensics team says the key document was generated.

events.title: An old arrest record
events.body: A local reporter has a 1976 arrest record: you, twenty-two, a traffic stop, a night in a county jail. It is true, and it is five days from the debate prep you needed.

choices.label: Confirm it and apologise
choices.text: Honest and quick: −0.4 nationally.

choices.label: Attack the timing and the source
choices.text: If it works, the story becomes their dirty trick.

result.lose: It became a week of stories

choices.label: Say nothing
choices.text: Let it burn out: −0.8 nationally.

events.title: The last word
events.body: One more speech, run on every channel for the last week. Choose how you want to be remembered.

choices.label: Optimism
choices.text: +0.6 nationally, +3 Momentum.

choices.label: Contrast
choices.text: +0.4 nationally; their momentum stalls.

choices.label: Fear
choices.text: +1.0 nationally, unless it backfires.

events.title: President {leader_last}
events.sub: The {party} Party holds the White House with {ev_you} electoral votes, {senate} senators and {house} representatives. The map stays on the table: now you govern it.

events.title: President {rival_last}
events.sub: The {rival_party} Party takes the White House. Your party holds {senate} Senate seats and {house} in the House. The 2002 midterms start now.

events.title: Form your cabinet
events.body: Cabinet secretaries are your great people in office: their ratings shape their departments for years. A unity pick from outside your coalition wins approval and costs your factions.

events.title: The lights go out in California
events.body: Rolling blackouts across the state; wholesale power prices up tenfold since last spring; traders gaming a market nobody fully understood. The governor wants federal price caps.

choices.label: Impose federal price caps
choices.text: The blackouts ease; the free-market wing is furious.

choices.label: Investigate the traders
choices.text: Slow, popular, and right: +1.5 in California; it takes a year.

choices.label: Let the market sort it out
choices.text: The base cheers; California does not.

events.title: What to do with the surplus
events.body: The budget office projects $5.6 trillion of surpluses over ten years. Every faction has a plan for it. Your first law sets the tone.

choices.label: Cut taxes across the board
choices.text: The Tax Cut becomes your first law, with a head start.

choices.label: A drug benefit for seniors
choices.text: The Medicare Drug Benefit becomes your first law, with a head start.

choices.label: Pay down the debt
choices.text: No law yet. Approval +2; the factions shrug.

events.title: A warning on the desk
events.body: The counter-terrorism chief has been trying to get this in front of the new administration since the transition: a terrorist network is planning a major attack inside the United States. History has it on the calendar for September. History is a default, not a law.

lines.label: Chance of a major attack on U.S. soil

events.advice: Cheap measures taken early are worth more than expensive ones taken late. The Aviation Security Act is on the White House's list of laws.

choices.label: Convene the principals this week
choices.text: Make it the first priority: −12 points on the forecast.

choices.label: Ask for a fuller report
choices.text: Prudent, and slow.

choices.label: Demand hearings
choices.text: In opposition, all you can do is make noise: −6 on the forecast; accused of politicising intelligence (−0.2).

choices.label: Keep it quiet
choices.text: Do not use intelligence for politics.

events.title: A spy plane down in China
events.body: A U.S. Navy surveillance plane has collided with a Chinese fighter over the South China Sea. The Chinese pilot is missing; the damaged plane landed on Hainan Island, and its twenty-four crew are being held.

choices.label: Express regret, carefully worded
choices.text: The crew come home in eleven days; hawks call it an apology.

choices.label: Demand the crew back, no apology
choices.text: Firm. It works fast or it does not.

result.win: The crew are home in a week

choices.label: Back the President, quietly
choices.text: Politics stops at the water's edge: +2 Momentum.

choices.label: Call it a humiliation
choices.text: Hawks love it (+10); swing voters wince (−0.2).

events.title: "Determined to strike"
events.body: The daily brief carries a warning in its title: the network is determined to strike inside the United States. Field offices have flagged men at flight schools. The forecast stands at {threat}%.

choices.label: Order a summer surge
choices.text: Airports, visas, the flight-school leads: −15 on the forecast, −1 approval.

choices.label: Make the agencies share what they have
choices.text: FBI and CIA in one room: −8 on the forecast.

choices.label: Note it and move on
choices.text: It is August.

choices.label: Go public with the warnings
choices.text: −5 on the forecast; −0.3 nationally for alarmism.

choices.label: Stay silent
choices.text: Nothing changes.

events.title: Attack on America
events.sub: Hijacked airliners strike the World Trade Center and the Pentagon; a fourth crashes in Pennsylvania. Nearly three thousand people are killed. The country rallies to its President.

events.title: Plot foiled
events.sub: Nineteen men are in custody after a coordinated sweep of flight schools and airports. Most Americans will never know how close it came; the people who stopped it do.

events.title: The end of the beginning
events.body: Two years in. {year_end_line} The 2002 midterms are eleven months away, and the century has forty-seven years to go.

choices.label: Close the year
choices.text: See the record, and what comes next.
